THE SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES OF MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT ACT, 

1954 ( 30 -of 1964 ). 


AN 
ACT 


to provide for the salaries and allowances of Members of Parliament. 
Be it enacted by Parliament in the Fifth Year of the Republic of India as follows : 
. 1. Short title and commencement. --( 1) This Act may be called the Salaries 
and Allowances of Members of Parliament Act , 1954 . 

(2 ) It shall come into force on the first day of June, 1954 . 
2. Definitions. In this Act, - 

(atracornmittee moans & Committee of either House of Parliament, and includes 
a Joint Committee of both Houses; 

(6 ) member means a member of either House of Parliament, but does not 
include 

( ) & Minister as defined in the Salaries and Allowances of Ministers 
Act , 1952 ( LVIII of 1952 ) ; and 

(ii) an officer of Parliament as defined in the Salaries and Allowancus 
of Officers of Parliament Act, 1953 ( 20 of 1933 ) ; 

(e) new member means a member who takes his seat in either House of 
Parliament after the commencement of this Aot and includes & member who is 
re-elected or re- nominated ; 

( d ) period of residence on duty means the period during which a member 
resides at a place where a session of a House of Parliament or a sitting of a 
committee is held or where any other business connected with his duties as such 
member is transacted , for the purpose of attending such session or sitting or 
for the purpose of attending to such other business, and includes 

(*) in the case of a session of a House of Parliament, a period of 
such residence , not exceeding three days, immediately preceding the commence 
ment of the session and a period of such residence, not exceeding three 
days, immediately succeeding the end of the session, and 

( ii) in the case of & sitting of a committee or any other business, 
a period of such residence, not exceeding two days, immediately preceding 
the commencement of the business of the committee or other business and 
& period of such residence, not exceeding two days, immediately succeeding 
the conolusion of the business of the committee or other business ; 

Explanation .-A member who ordinarily resides at a place where a session 
of a House of Parliament or a sitting of a Committee is held or where any 
other business connected with his duties as such member is transacted shall , 
for the duration of the session or sitting or the time ocoupied for the transao 
tion of other business ( including the three or two days immediately preceding 
or suoceeding ), be deemed to reside at sich place for the purpose of attending 
such session or sitting of , as the case may be for the purpose of attending to 
such other business ;

3. Salaries and daily allowanca . --A member shall be entitled to receive 
a salary at the rate of four hundred rupees per mensem during the whole of his 
torm of office plus an allowance at the rate of twenty -one rupees for each day 
during any period of residence on duty . 

4. Travelling allowancos. -- (1) There shall be paid to each member in respeot 
of every journey performed by hina for the purpose of attending a session of a House 
of Parliament or a meeting of a Committee or for the purpose of attending to any 
other businoss connected with his duties as a member, from his usual place of 1 esi

business is to be transacted and for the return journey from such place to his

(a ) if the jouroey is performed by rail, an amount equal to one second 
class fare plus one third class fare for each such journey , irrespective of the 
class in which the member actually travels ; 

(6 ) if the journey is perfurmed by air , an amount equal to one and one 
fourth of the air fare fyr each such journey ; 
(0 ) if the journey or any part thereof cannot be performed by rail or air 

(i) where the journey or any part thereof is performed by steamer, 
an amount equal to one and three - fifths of the fare ( without diet ) for the 
highest class in the steainer for each such journey or part thereof ; 

( ii ) where the journey or any part thereof is performed by road , a 
road mileage at the rate of eight annas per mile for each such journey or 

part thereof. 
Explanation . - For the purposes of sub - clause ( ii ) of clause (c) of this sub -section , 
the expression journey shall inolude the journey from and to the railway station , 
port or aerodrome to and from the usual place of esidence of the werber or as 
the case may be , the residence of the member at th place where the session of 
the House of Parliament or a meeting of the Committee is to be held or where 
any other business is to be transacted . 

2 Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), a member who per

admissible to him it he had travelled by rail or steamer , as the Ouse may be :

NEW YEARS MESSAGE FOR 1950 OF JUSTICE EMIL SANDSTREM CHAIRMAN 

OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS, LEAGUE OF RED CROSS SOCIETIES. 

The year 1954 witnessed the guth annivorsary of the first National Red Cross 
Societies to be founded after Henri Dunant s inspired jdea - the setting into action 
of a world -wide movement direoted towards tho alleviatwn of the suffering of war 
viotims began , in 1864 , to take form and shape. A year earlier - 1863 -the first Geneva 
Convention had been signed and the International Committee of the Red Cross 
tounded. The Belgian Red Cross was the first National Society to appear on the 
scene : 72 others have since followed in its footsteps, and today constitute the or 
ganisation which was the aim of its founder . 

If on this occasion we stop to ask ourselves to what extent the Red Cross has 
fulfilled the intentions of Henri Dunant, only one answer is possible : like everything 
human , this institution may have its faults , but its value , indeed its necessity , have 
been fully demonstrated . 

What the Red Cross has done , i. e . the various National Societies , the Interna 
tional Committee of the Red Cross , and the League of Red Cross Societies, in times 
of war -which alus, have been only too frequent -aod in war s aftermath , not to mention 
its no less important work between war a , are ample evidence that Honri Dunant s 
idea was no less than & prophetio vision . The volunteer wurkers of the Red Crops 
have carried out the task expected of them ; they bave shown the world how much 
way be schieved in the humanitarian field by men of goodwill, whon love of neigh 
bour is the guiding force , and efforts are .coordinated by a suitable organisation , 


MANIPUR GAZETTE , JANUARY 8 , 1988 . 


With the opening up of new spheres of activity in time of peace and with 
the tragic increase in the number of natural disasters of recent years , especially 
the year just past , the importance of the Read Cross and its misson in the world 
are to -day greater than ever . 

In paying tribute to all that was achieved by the founder of the movement 
and by our predecessors , we look also to the future , determined to carry out our 
dnty to do our share of the work which lies ahead . 

In this I know I am expressing what you yourselves feel. On the threshold 
of the New Year, I want to say " Thank you " to the Red Cross Societies and their 
members, to the friends of the Red Cross, for the efforts that have been made 
during the past year, and to give you my best wishes for a Happy New Year, 
bringing success in your work and the contentment that comes from the sense of 
having done one s duty .

PRESS NOTE 


Imphal, the 30th December, 1954 . 
The following letter No. E /127- A / 172 dated 21-12-54 received from the Asstt . 
Reoruiting Officer , Shillong Military Exchange regarding Auxiliary Territorial Force 
at Imphal is republished for general information . 

G. H. Singh , 
Publicity Officer , Manipur . 


Subject : - Auxiliary Territorial Force Training at Imphal. 
1. Auxiliary Territorial Force Training Camp will be held at Imphal from 16 
January 55 to 26 January 65 . 

2. The strength of the camp will be 480 volunteers . The trainees of last year 
camp aro also eligible to undergo training this year. 

3. A recruiting party will be visiting Imphal sometime in the first week of 
January 55 , the firm date will be intimated to you when approved by the higher 
authorities and recruitment will be carried out daily from 0800 hrs , to 1300 hrs . 
The last year s trainees who are willing to undergo training this year as well, are 
required to inform the Officer Communding Auxiliary Territorial Force Camp or 
Assistant Recruiting Officer c/o Imphal Dak Bunglow on or before 11 January 1955 . 
After this date their cages may not be considered . 

4. All able -bodied Indian Citizen who are between 17 to 40 years of age are 
eligible for enrolment in the Auxiliary Territorial Force. The training will com 
mence from 16 January 55 to 25 January 55 ( both days inclusive ). During the 
training period the trainees will stay in the camp under military discipline and 
will be provided free food and accommodation and on completion of training they 
will be paid Rs. 5 /- as pocket allowance. 

5. Ex -servicemen and NCC Cadets and personal beloning to Police Department 
are not eligible for recruitment . 

Illigible , 
Assistant Recruiting Officer.

published in the Manipur State Gazette 

$ d / -- T. Kipyen ,

No. F. 12 ( 2 )/ J / 11 /55 . 


NOTIFICATION . 


Ministry of Home Affairs 


New Delhi , dated the 26th April , 1955 . 


In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 2 of the Part C States (Laws) 
Act , 1950 ( XXX of 1950 ), the Central Government hereby extends to the State of 
Manipur the Code of Criminal Procedure , 1898 ( Act V of 1898 ), as at present in 
force in the State of Assam , with the following restrictions and modifications, 
namely- (a ) throughout the said Code, references to the State Government shall be 
construed as references to the Chief Commissioner, (b ) in Se.ition 1, for sub - section 
( 2) , the following shall be substituted , namely— " ) It extends to the whole of India 
except the State of Jammu and Kaslımir , but in the absence of any specific pro 
vision to the contrary , nothing herein contained shall affect the Manipur State Courts 
Act, 1917 , or the Manipur State Hill Peoples ( Administration ) Regulation , 1947 , or 
any order spacial or local law now in the State of Manipur , or any special juris 
diction or power conferred or any special form of Procedure prescribed , by any 
other law for the time being in firce ." (c) For the purpose of facilitating the 
application of the said Code in the State of Manipur, any court or other authority 
may construe the said Code with such alterations, not affecting the substance , as 
may be necessary or proper to adapt it to the matter before the court or other 
authority . 

Sd - A. V. Pai, 

Secretary

No. H.Apptt.31 !51.- The following Resolution received from the Government of 
India , Ministry of Home Affairs , is published for general information . : -- 

T. Kipgen , 

Secretary to the Govt . of Manipur . 
New Delhi- 2 , the 30th April, 1955 . 

RESOLUTION . 
No. 15 / 1 /55 - 

ST. 
In order to secure greater representation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled 
Tribes in the public services, the maximum age- limit prescribed for appointment to 
a non -Gazetted service or post wis increased by five years in the case of candidates 
belonging to these Castes and Tribes vide Government of India , Ministry of Home 
Affairs Resolution No. 42/ 19 / 51- NGS dated the 25th June, 1952 . It has now been 
decided that this concession should be extended to appointments to gazetted posts 
in the ( entral Services. The applications of these orders to recruitment to All - India 
Services is separately under consideration . 

2. The above decision will take ellect immediately . The Union Public Service 
Commission VA agreed that where the advertisements issued by them require that 
applications from candidates should reach the Commission on a date falling within 15 
days from the date of this Resolution , the last date for the receipt of applications 
from Scheduled Ciste and Scheduled Tribe candidates will be extended by two weeks. 
Other recruiting authorities for posts under the Government of India will also 
take similar action wherever necessary . 

Sd /- G. Swaminathan , 
Joint Socy . 10 the Govt . of India .

invited for the exclusive right to exiract and trade in Cane from Manipur Stilte 
Forests and will be recived by the undersigued upto 2 1. M. on the 24th May , 
1955. The period of contract is commencing from 1st June , 1950 ending on : Ist 
Marcb , 1937 . 

Each tenderer must deposit an earnest muny of lis . 50 /- (Rupees fifty) only 
either in the Imphal Treasury or Silchar Treasury which will be refunded in case 
of unsuccessful tenders and will be convertel into caution money in case of success 
ful tenders . The copy of the Trea - ury Chalan slioule lie enchised in the tender 
failing wlich the tender should be rejected. Each tender should state the luinp sum 
monopoly fee which he is prepared tu pay for this right for the above period. 

In addition to the monopoly fee , royalty on canes actually extracted should 
be paid according to the Schedule rates fixed by the Assam Forest Department. Suc 
C :ssful tenderers should execute an agreement within 10 days of the receipt of 
information to that effect and shall pay monoply fee at the time of signing the 
lease failing which the tender shall be treated as cancelled and earnest juoney deposited 
will be forfeited to the State . 

The Cane Mahal of the State is divided int , three separato Mahals as follows 
and each one should be tendered for separately .

Irang and Tuijang . 

(Mahal No. III.)

money ) ওই ইম্ফাল ট্রেজমিদা খম্বিদননি অমসুং চালান কপি অমা টোগা লােইন পিবিগদবনি । 

চালান 
অসি যাদব। টেঙার অমতা লৌজরােই । ফাওদবা টেণ্ডারগীদি আরনে মনি অদু হলোকচগণি । অফাওবা টেণ্ডারগীদি 
সিকুরিটি ( Security ) গী শরুক অম । ওই লৌবস্ত যাই । 

টেণ্ডারারনা মহাক্কী টেঙার অদু আৰে হায় সুমিত্তগী চয়ো অমগী মনুংদা পটা সহি তেবিরা পাঠাগী 
মতুংইন্না থবক তৌবিপদবনি । পাটা সহি তৌবা মিত্তা লুপা ১০০ দগী লুপা ৫০০, ফাওবা পি রেভি ষ্টোনগনা 
লুপ ৫০ , (য়াথৈ) অমসুং লুপ , ৫০০ দগী হেনবনা লুপা ১০০ (চামা ) ট্রেজারি চালান ওই জামিন ( Security ) 
থগিদলনি । জামিন অসি পাটাগী মতম লেইরগ শেলোই য়াওদনা হলোকচানি । পাটাদানা করিওম্বা সবকারগী 
অতােনবা শেল লৈরবদি জামিন অসিদগী করুগা সরকারগী অতােনবা শেল অদু উশল তৌগনি, করিও জামিলা 
লৈরিবা শেলনা অতেন অদু কুপখৎপা শুদ্ৰবদি লৌ ইম্বোল খাজনা তােগা লৌখৎনব । নিয়ম মতুংইন্না সরকারগী 
শেন্দোল উশল তৌগনি । 
৫। শ্বাইদগী শেল অহেনবা নত্রবসু কনাগুম্বা অমগী টেণ্ডার লৌবগী ক্ষমতা শ্রীযুক্ত ফোরেষ্ট আফিসারগীনি । 

টোরদা পিরিবা মমল অদুনা মতিক চাদে খল্লবদি রেভি ষ্টেশনশিং অসি তারিখ ১২৫৫৫ ইংদা ফোরেষ্ট 
অফিস নিলাম তৌদুনা মােনগনি । 

৭। দুপা ৫০০ , ( চামঙ ) দগী হেনবা রেভিনু ষ্টেসনগীদি কিস্তি মরিবক্তা থিবা আগনি । অসিৎপা শেলগী তথ্যই অমা 
যােন সুমিতা অহাবা কিস্তি ওইনা থিৱগা লেনহেবা অদুনা চপ মান্ননা কিস্তি ৩ লজ্জা লােইনা থিগদবনি । নুপা ৫০০ , 
( চামঙ ) অমসুং অদুদগী তাবা মমলদি যােবা সুমিত্তা শুনা থিবিগবনি । 

নিলামদা অমসুং টেণ্ডালদা শিৎপা শেলগ মথা অনৌবা সরকারগী নিয়ম মতুংইন্না শেল টেক্স ( sale tax ) লুপা ১ 
দা পৈশা ২ ( অনি) গী হিংদা অমুক পিগদবনি ।

No 1 of 1955 


L HOVITICATED 11 


THE PUESIDENT IS TIL : FIFT YEAR OF JE REPUBLIC Or Ixpia . 


An Ordinance to provide , in the interests of the gonoral public , for the control of 

the production , supply and distribution of, and trude and comnicrce in , certain 
commodities. 

WIIEREAS the Essential Supplies ( Temporary Powers) Act, 1946 (XXIV of 1946 ), 
which confers powers to control the production , supply and distribution of and trade 
and commerce in , certain commodities, expires on the 26th day of January , 1955 ; 

AND WHEREAS it is necessary, in the interests of the general public , to provide 
for the continuance of such powers in relation to some of the commodities specified 
in that Act and certain , other coiumuditics ; 

AS WHERTAS Parliament is not in session and the President is satisfied that 
circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action ; 

Noll , TIERLTORE , in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (1) of article 123 
of the Constitution , the President is pleased to promulgate the following Ordinance : 

1. Short title, extent and commencemont.- ( 1) This Ordinance may be called 
the Essential Commodities Ordinance , 1955 . 

(9) It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir . 
(3 ) It shall come into force on the 26th day of January , 1955 . 
2. Definitions. -- In this Ordinance , unless the context otherwise requires , - 
(« ) " essential commodity ” means any of the following classes of commodities : 

( ) coal, including coke and other derivatives ; 
( ii) component parts and accessories of antomobiles ; 
( iii) cotton and woollen textiles 
(iv ) iron and steel , including manufutured products of iron and steel ; 
(1 ) paper , including newsprint, paper board and straw board ; 
( vi ) petroleum and petroleum produrts ; 
(vii ) șalt ; 
(viii) sugar ; 
(ix ) vanaspari ; 

(1 ) veetable oil ;

being a commodity with rarp.ct to which Pırliiment hi 19 power to m ko laws by 
virtuo of entry 33 in List JIL in th : Seventh Schedule to the Constitution ;

(c ) “ State Government" in relation to it part C St:ut means the Lieutenant 

Governor or the Chief Commissioner, as the case may be .

No. PYII-863( 30 ) /55 . 


Imphal, the 31st May , 1955 . 
No. CS /3 / 55. - In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 3 of the Esgontial 
Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955 ) and with the previous concurrence of the Central 
Government , the Chief Commissioner of Manipur is pleased to make the following Order : 

Manipar Foodgrains (Movement) Control Order , 1955 . 
1 . Short title , commencement and application . 

(a ) This Order may be called the " Manipur Foodgrains (Movement) Control 

Order , 1955. 

(b ) It shall come into force forthwith and extend to the whole of Manipur. 
2. Definitions. 
( 1 ) " Foodgrains" for the purpose of this order means “ Rice , paddy and products" 

thereof . 
(2) " Rice and paddy produots " include Chira , Muri, Khoi , Broken rice and 

any article whatsoever which originally comes from paddy excepting husk 
and bbusi. 


2 


MANIPUR GAZETTE , MAY 31, 1955 . 


3. (a ) No person shall export or attempt to export any Foodgrains from Manipur 
to any place outside Manipur, except under and in accordance with a permit issued 
loy the State Government or any officer authoris3d by the State Government in 
this behalf . 

(b ) No person shall transport, attempt to transport, cause to be transported 
or offer for transport any Foodgrains into the area of the State lying to the north 
of the village Kangpokpi except under and in accordance with a permit issued by 
the St: te Government in this behalf. 

Provided nothing in clause (a ) and (b ) above shall apply to tho export or trans 
port of Foodgrains - 

(i) not exceeding five secrs in weight in aggregate by a bonafide tra 

veller as a part of his luggage . 
( ii ) or ( overnment account. 

( iii ) under and in accordance with Military credit notes. 
4. Any Police Officer not below the rank of Assistant Sub - inspector and any 
other person authorised in this behalf by the State Government may with a view 
to securing compliance with this order 

(a ) stop , seurch , or authoriso any person to stop and search any person , 
boat, motor or any vehicle or receptacle used or capable of being used for the 
transport of Foodgrains ; 

(1 ) inter aod search or authorise any person to enter and search any place . 

( c ) seize or authorise the seizure of any article in respect of which he suspects 
that a contravention of this Order has been , is being or is about to be committed 
along with the packages , coverings or receptacles in which such articly is found 
or the animals , vehicles, vessels or conveyances 

conveyances used in carrying such article 
and there fter take or authorise the taking of all the measures necessary for 
securing the production of tho articles, packages, coverings, receptacles or animals , 
vehicles , vessels , or conveyances so seized , in it court and for their safe custody 
pending such production . 
5. If any person contravenes the provisions of this Order, then 

then without pre 
judice to any other punishment to which he may be liable the court unay direct : 

( a ) that any property in respect of which the offence has been committed 
or a part thereof shall be forfeited to the Government ; 

(b ) that the packages, coverings or receptacles in which any property liablo 
to be forfeited has been found and the animals, vehicles , vessels or the oonveyances 
used in carrying the said articles shall be forfeited to Government. 

Provided that no court shall declare any such package, covering or recep 
tacle or any such animal, vehicle , vessel or other conveyance forfeited to Government 
unless it is proved that the owner theroof knew that the offence was being or 
was to be or was likely to be committed .

( SCHOLARSHIPS AND INFORMATION DIVISION ) 
SUBJECT : Particulars regarding 3 scholarships offered to Indian nationals by the 

Government of Italy . 
The Government of Italy have offered 3 scholarships tonable in Italy for a 
period of one year during 1955-56 to Indian nationals includiny. 

(a ) Scholars desiring advanced post -graduate study /research work /specialised 
practical training in the following fields : 

(i) Any engineering or techvological field . 
( ii ) Any basic Science or Art subject. 

( iii ) Education etc. 
( b ) Artists who wish to complete their outlook in contact with Italian 

surroundings. 
(c) Technicians who wish to specialise at Agricultural institutes ( for vine 

growing , olive- tree growing , tobacco growing etc. ), Industrial Institutes 
( for textiles , graphic arts , ch sinicals etc. ) and Experimental Centres (for 

the growing of rice and graios). 
Scholarships are meant for postgraduate studies/ Research work and advanced 
practical training in the fields anumerated above. Those possessing the Master s 
degree in Arts /Science /Education or a degree in Engineering /Agriculture/ Technology or 
diploma in Art are eligible to apply . 

Preference will be given to the candidates knowing Italian . Can.lidates knowing 
French will also be considered favourably . University studies start November 
1st, 1955 and the selected candidates would be expected to leave for Italy in thu 
first week of Octob -r. While selecting the candidates, such personal qualities as make 
him /her specially fit for promotion of international understanding would be considered 
as a necessary qualification . 

The value of the scholarship is 50,000 Lire per mensem (Rs. 382 approx ). In 
Addition selected scholars will receive an allowance of 10.000 Lire (Rs. 76 approx ) 
for any other expenses which they might have to incur in Italy . 

University fees which the scholar may be required to pay will als ) be refunded 
to them . 

Sea passage expenses by 2nd / Touri-t class from India to Italy and back will be 
provided by the Government of India to the selected scholars . 
The candidates are required to send the following along with their applicatijns : 

(i) Two pass- port size photographs with the signature of the candi 

datry on the reverse . 
( ii) Attested copies of certificates/diplomas/degrees in respect of the 

qualification claimed (not returnable ) . 
(iii ) Detailed programme of study which the candidate intends to 

undertake in Italy . 


on 


MANIPUR GAZETTE , JUNE 1 , 1955 . 


7 


( iv ) The curriculum of studies already completed . 
( v ) Health certificate from Registered Medical Practitioner that 

the candidate is of sound physical constitution . 
Prescribed application forms etc. can be had from the Ministry of Education 
( Scholarships and inforination Division ) Section S / 1 New Delhi, The last date for 
the receipt of applications in the Ministry of Education is 20th June, 1955. No 
application will be considered without a fee of Rs. 5 ( Rs . 1/4 /- in the of 
Scheduled Cates, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes) which should be sent 
through the postal order along with application in favour of the Ministry of 
Education , Government of India , New Delhi.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA SCIIOLARSHIPS TO INDIAN NATIONALS FOR 

SPECIALISATION IN FOREIGN LANG AGES ABROAD) - 1950-530 


The Govt. of India have decided to award in 1955-56 , 30 scholi rships tenable 
alsroad to Indian natii n ils for specialising in Arabic , Chinese , French , German , 
Italian , Japanese, Persian , Spanish , Turki-h and Russian . 

Only candidates sponsored and recommended by the Universities /comparable insti 
tutions/ Central or State ( ovts. who are prepired to serve the -ponsoring authorities 
for at least thrrin years after their return to India will be considered . They should 
have a good University deyree and except for awards in Spanish , Italian , Turkis ), 
and Japanese languages should have already studied the language concerned and 
acquired profici-ncy therein , Candidates for Scholarships in Spanish , Italian , Turkish , 
and Japanese languages should have clementary knowledg : or aptitude for the 
foreign language concerned . Candidates should not be 

than forty years 


more 


of age . 


The scholarships will be normally tenable for one year and will cover mainte 
nance and cost of travel. 

l rescribed application forms and further particulars can be had from the Spon 
soring Authorities or from the Government of India , Miristry of Education , Scholir 
ships and Information Division ( Section S. 1), New Delhi. The last date for the 
receipt of applications is the 15th July , 1955 . 


Imphal, the 30th May , 1955 . 
The Government of India have provided a sum of Rs. 1,30,00,000; - for the 
year 195.5-56 to award scholarships to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other 
Backward Classes . The scholarships are tenable in recognised lostitutions in India 
imparting education beyond the Matriculation stage in the following courses men 
tioned in order of preference . 

(a ) Medicine and allied subjects including Nursing . 
( b ) Engineering and Architecture . 
(c) Agriculture, Forestry and Veterinary Science . 
(d ) Technology . 
( e ) Science. 
(f ) Education and Social Service . 
(g ) Humanities including Arts ). Social Science , Fine Arts and Languages. 
(h ) Commerce . 

(i) Law and Library Science . 
The last date of receiving applichlijns by the Ministry of Education , New Delbi 
is 31st July , 1951. Particulars of the amount of scho arships, instruction to candi 
dates , regulations and application forms may be obtained in the Offices of the 
Superintendent (Home Office ), the Sub-divisional Officers , the Principal , D. M. College, 
the Inspector of Schools , the Chief Medical Officer , the Director of Agriculture, 
the Forest Officer and the Executive Engineer, Manipur P.W.D., Imphal.

Subject : CAR FESTIVALS OF 1955 . 
The Car festivals of Lord Jaganath at Puri will be celebrated from the 5th of 
Junc, 1955 and will continue till the 4th of July , 19 5. This festival, Susila , 
will attract large numbers of pilgrins from all over India . It is observed that 
epidemics of cholera break out either during or after the festival. stw sporadie 
cases of cholera aro being reported froin some parts of Oristband also from neighbouring 
States , particularly from hordering States, it is felt that the intending pilgrims 
should be advised through newspapers and other sources to yut.themselves protected 
ayainst cholera sufficiently in advance . 

Adequate medical and public health arrangements are being undertaken in this 
State on the occasion but as mentioned before , it is vesirable thit this pilgrims, 
intènding : to visit Puri from your State should set them - elves inocula ed and obtain 
necessarys inoculation certificate , as otherwise they will not be allowed to enter into 
the festival areas without such inoculation certificite . Temporary regulatione mahing 
cholera inoculation conspulsory in the festival area under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 
1897 from 15th of April 1953 to 15th July , 1955 arc boing enforced lloil ers of 
certificates of inoculation issued after 1-4-55 will however not be required to take 
further inoculation in the festival area .

নিলাম নােটিশ নং ৪ । 


তাং ২৪।৫।৫৫ ইং । 


অসিনা পাৎকী পাটাদারশি : অমসুং মনিপুৰ প্ৰজা পুমা খঙলি । 

মৰমদি ;--- খাদা ইলিব পাৎকী পাটাদার শিং মশােই নখখাইনা তাং ১৫৫৫৫ ই , ফাওবদা খীফম খােপ অনবা 
কিস্তী খীৰদবা নগা শুনা খাবগীদমক লেমথোরিবা মতম, তাং ৩১৩৫৬ ইং ফাওবা চান পাশিং অসি তাং ২৮৬৫৫ 
ইং লেপাপােকপা মুমিৎকী অমুক পুং ১১ তাবদগ হৌন ডিপুটি কমিশনার আফিসদা মখাগী করাশি; অসিগী মতুংইন্না 
অমুকন্না নিলাম তৌদুনা য়োনগনি । 

( ক ) নিলাম ওকপিলা মীনা নিলাম মফম গাছ । এক লিবা পালিগী : সিকুরিটি ( গমিন ) গা অহানব । কিস্তি, 
পাৎমলগা শরুক , গা পুন্না থাশিগদলনি ; শোয়বা খল পাৎ অপু অমুক হন্না নিলাম তৌধু সেনগনি । অকোনবা নিলাম 
অসিদা পাগল হলদি হৰিবা শেল অদু হান্না •িলাম একপা মানা হাপকংকদবনি । 

( খ ) নিলাণ একপা শুনিৎ ৭ নিগী মনুদা সিকুরিটিগী শকক অদু পংলগী শরুক : শুনবা পকংকলনি । অলােইবা 
কিস্তিনা তাং ৩১৭৫৫ ইং ফাওবা খাবিনি । শোহরবাদ ২ান্না খাখিবা শেল পুম্নমক মলগা পাৎ অমুক হন্না লিলাম 
তৌবা যাই । 
( গ) নিসান রিবা আফিসানা খাইদগী চানো দা নওগ। কলি ও দাগ অ লৌদব নাই 

অদুগা পাংকুশল 
পীররা পা দু লিন পুপোক্তৰ আই । 

( ঘ) নিলাম অমি রাগী একেইবা কৃদি চীফ কমিশনাবনা লেপকনি । 


R. C. Chaulhury . 
Doputy Comunissioner, Manipur.

No. TM /10/55 /8. — Consequent on the separation of accounts from audit in respect 
of Foud , Rehabilitation and Supply Departments of the ſtoverument of India all payments 
relating to the Food , Rehabilitation and Supply Ministries of the Government of 
India from April , 1955 (Payable in May 55 ) ouwards will be made by the Separated Pay 
and Accounts Offices by Bank Drafts. Receipts rel.iting to these Departments will 
however, continue to be credited at the treasuries as before and such credits will 
be passed on to the Pay and Accounts Officers by this office weekly by means of 
Bank Drafts . 


In Order , therefore , to enable this office to settle the transictions on account 
of Food , Rehabilitation and Supply Ministries weekly with the Pay and Accounts 
Officer concerned the Treasury Officers in Assam , Tripura and Manipur are hereby 
requested to furnish this office with a statement showing the transactions relating 
to these ministries arising at their treasuries in Form T. A. 47 on the 8th , 16th 
24th and the last day of each month aocurding to the provisions of Art 117 of 
the Account Code, vol. II. 

S. N. Bhuyan , 
Aesistant Accountants Officer , Assam .

বাইবীগে হায়বদি মহাগী নিয়মশিং অসিগী মঙ্গুইন্না থবক তৌবীগদবনি । 

১। শামু অৱাইমন -বৰ নগা কন্যা শিজিনা ওইরগা লুপা ৩০, ( ক ) অদুগা বর-কন্যা অনিমকন

বালিঙৈদা অফিতা মতম চানা লাক্তনা মথা হায়রি রেট মতু ইন্না অইমন খিবিগদবনি ।

৩। কবিগুধা নােং - চিং তানা শামু হন খুদোং চাদ্ৰবদি মউৎকী চান -খবা পিবীগদবনি । 

৪। শামু বাইরম্নগা করিগুৰা যুম - কৈ মাংদুনা য়ৈথােক তারবদি খুদজা ( অফিস্তা) রিপাের্ট পিবীগদবনি ।

T. Kipgen , 

Secretary to the Government of Manipur . 
GENERAL CONDITIONS OF GRANT- IN - AID . 
1 . Every Aided School must be conducted in accordance with the Rules and 
Orders of the Education Departinent 

2 . The curricula , as notified from time to time by the Education Department , 
must be followed and text bouks selected from the list of approved text books. 

3. The appointment, confirmation and dismissal of teachers must be approved , 
in the case of High Schools by the Inspector of Schools , and in the case of schools 
of lower grade by the Deputy Inspector of Schools. 

In the latter case an appeal may be made to the Inspector of Schools whose 
decision shall bo final. 

4. No buikling operations must be undertaken until the plans and estimates 
have been * pproved by the Department. 

5. All receipts and disbursements must be entered in the account books of the 
school which shall be open to examination by any authorised officer and copy 
of the audited accounts should be submitted annually to the Inspector of Schools. 

6. Grants will be paid inonthly on the basis of a statement in & prescribed 
form which shall be submitted by the school authority at the close of each month 
to the Inspector of Schools in the case of ligh Schools and schools enjoying 
special grants , to the Loputy Inspector in the case of Middle and Primary Schools. 

7. Grants are payable on bills drawn by the School authority in the prescribed 
form and countersigned by the Inspector of Schools in the case of High and special 
schools and by the Deputy Inspector of Schools in the case of Middle and Primary 
Schools . 

8. Surplus funds shall be placed in the Post Office Savings Bank or otherwise 
as approved by the Inspector of Schools . 

No part of the surplus fund shall be spent without the sanction of the Inspector 
of Schools except for payment of the sanctioned staff . 

9. Government may clainn a fair sba ! e of any balance at the credit of an aided 
school on its abolition as well as of the sale proceeds of any building, furniture or 
other property for which a grant may bave been made. 

10. The rate of pay fixed by a school, for its teaching staff must receive the 
approval of the countersigning authority . 

11. The percentage of students passing the Matriculation Examination of u particular 
High School should not fall below prescribed minimum percentage for three consecutive 
years . 

12. No teacher of an aided Institution shall take part in party or other politics. 
Participation in politics shall include : 

( a) Holding an office, paid or honorary , in party organisation including 

men bership of the Executive Committee . 
(b ) Addressing political meetings . 
(c ! Conducting election campaigns. 

( d ) Taking part in strikes , demonstrations and the like. 
13. Discipline should be properly maintained in the schcol. 

14. Grant - in - aid will be liable to be withdrawn for breach of any of the above . 
oonditions .

Subject :-Change of nomenclature of certain Sections of Accounts . 
Notification No. TM / 10 /55 / 11.-- It is hereby notified for the guidance and informa 
tion of all the treasury and sub - treasury Officers in Assam , Manipur and Tripura 
that the President has approved the opening of a new section in accounts viz . 
“ NA - Inter State Debt Settlements " within the consolidated Fund of India or State 
with the followiny major heads : 

(i) India & Pakist.in . 
(ii ) India & Burma , 
( iii ) Madras and Andhra . 

( iv ) Madras and Mysore . 
The above major heads will close to “ Government " in the ledger. 

The President has also approved that with effect from the Current Financial 
Year (1955-56 ) the existing Sections. “ Y - Public Debt to ” V - Cash Balance may be 
re -arranged with new guide letters as follows . 

CONSOLIDATED FUND . 
N. - Public Debt. 
0. — Loans and Advances by the Central Government . 
P. - Loans and Advances by State Governments . 
G. - loter State Debt Settlements . 

PUBLIC ACCOUNT 
R.- Unfunded Debt. 
S. - Deposits and Advances 
T ..- Remittances. 
U. - Transfer of cash between England & India . 
V.- Reserve Bank Deposits . 
W.- Cash Balance . 

S. N. Bhuyan , 
Assistant Accounts Officer .

Sub) .- Particulars regarding a scholarship offered to an Indian national by the Government 

of Switzerland . 

1. The Government of Switzerland have offered one scholarship for a period 
of one year during 1955-56 to an Indian national for higher Study / Research / in any 
branch of Science / Technology /Engineering at any of the Swiss Universities , research 
establishments or similar Institutions of higher learning . 

2. Other terms and conditions . 


( i ) The amount of scholarship is 500-700 Swiss Frances ( France = 1.089 

Rupees ) p.m. the amount will be fixed by the Swiss Government 
according to the academic standard of the candidate and the pro 

granume for his studies . 
( ii ) Exemption from tuition fees . 
( iii ) The cost of tourist class Sea passage expenses from India to Switzer 

land and back will be provided by the Govt. of Iudia . 
( iv ) Selection candidate is expected to reach Switzerland in the beginning 

of October , 19.15 . 
3. Tbose possessing Master s degree in Science or a degree or equiralent qualification 
in Engineering / Technology from a recognised university are eligible to apply. Candidates 
above 35 years of age on 1st August , 1955 will not be considered . 

4. Preference will be given to the candidates knowing German or French language . 
While selecting the candidate, such personal attributes as make him /her especially 
fit for furtherance of international understanding would be considered as necessary 
qualifications. 

5. The candidates are required to send the fullowing documents along with 
their applications : 

( i ) Two pass - port siza photographs with the signature of the candidate 

on the reverse . 
( ii ) Attested copies of certificates /diplomas/degrees iu respect of the 

qualification claimed ( not returnable ) . 
( iii ) Detailed programme of study which the candidate intends to under 

take in Switzerland . 
( iv ) The curriculum of studies already completed . 
( v ) Health certificate from a Registered Medical Practitioner that the 

candidate is of sound physical constitution . 
Prescribed application forms etc. can be had from the Ministry of Education 
( Sobolarships and Inforination Division ) Section S - 1 New Delbi. The last date for 
the receipt of applications in the Ministry of Education is 20th July , 1956. No 
application will be considered without a fee of Rs. 5 ( Rs . 1 /4 /- in the case of 
Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes ) which should be sent 
through the postal order along with application in favour of the Ministry of Education , 
Govt. of India , New Delhi. Amount remitted through money order or cheque will 
not be accepted . 

Applications received after the prescribed date will not be giver any consideration.

Breediny (Rice) ( ii) Soil Science and Ayricultural Chemistry with specia

NOTIFICATION No. TM / 4 / 55 / 17 . 


Dated , Shillong , the 4th July , 1955 . 
Subject :- Extension of date for sending Advice for Inter -Government Adjustments 

to the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank of India . 
It is notified for information of all Treasury Officers and Sub - Treasury Officers 
and Departmental Disbursing Officers that all cash and bouk transactions involving 
inter -Governmental adjustments that originate towards the close of the year should 
be advised by the A. G. to the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank 
of India by the 15th April as required under Article 88 of the Account Code 
Vol. IV . But it has been observed that this due date could not be adhered to 
during last several years due to non -receipt of the returns from the Treasury and 
Departmental Disbursing Officers by the A. G. timely . 

All Treasury Ollicers and Departmental Disbursing Officers are , therefore, re 
quested to take special steps to submit all returns of inter-Governmental transac 
tion in advance so as to enable the A. G. to settle the transaction with the Reserve 
Bank of India by the due date . 

( C. A. G. s No. 567 -AC / 95-55 , dated 17-5-55 
Dy.CAG - 164 in TM.4 / 85 )

PRESS NOTE . 
INVITATION OF COMPENSATION APPLICATIONS 

Last date for filing September 26 , 1955 . 
lhe Central Government have published a rolification in the Gazette of India 
dated June 27 , 1955 under Section 4 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and 
Rehabilitation ) Act, 195+ inviting applications for compensation from all those dis 
placed persons with verified claims for immovable property left in West Pakistan , 
who have not applicd before under any of the priority categories or otherwise . 

Applications for compensation should be preferred in duplicate on the prescribed 
form and handed over or sent to the Settlement Officer within wbose juridiction 
the applicant resides, or carrits on business or works for gain . The prescribed forms 

on sale at all Settlement Offices under the Central Ministry of Rehabilitation , 
and at Post Oflices. In addition to the various documents which form part of the 
applications, svery claimant should put in an allidavit in the form specified under 
the rules and attested by a Magistrate or an Oaths Commissioner or by any other 
officer competent to administer an oath , and sh uld also send three passport size 
photographs and a certified copy of the claim assessment order. Applicants are re 
quired to give full details of loans, etc. owing from them as also arrears of rent. 
Under the rules, severe penalties aru prescribed for falso information given in regard 
to these public durs. 

Thoso claimants who have already sent in their applications for compensation in 
the priority categories or in connection with the purchase of property, or the gran 
tiny of loans, or otherwise , need not apply again . 

In thosc cases where the original claimint has died and successors in interest 
now wish to put in applications for compeusation , they shwuld , in addition t the 
documents comprising the application form , alss submit particulars of the date and 
place of death of the deceased claimant with a duly certified death certificate and 
give particulars of heirs and relatives of the deceased and a true copy of the will 
or other document on which they rely . Such successors in interest will also have 
to swear an affidavit in support of their statements. 

R. F. A. loanees should obtain a certificate from the Rehabilitation Finance Admi 
nistration regarding the total amount duo from them as principal and interest as 
on June 30 , 1955 , and send this certificate along with their compensation applications. 

Applicants should fill in all the particulars required in the forms carefully so 
as to avoid delay which will be caused if inaccurato or incomplete information is given . 
The last date for the filing of compensation applications is September 26 , 1955. 

A list of Sttlement Officers all over India with their respective jurisdictions is 
given below for the guidance of applicants. 

Displaced persons with verified claims residing outside India , who have not already 
applied , should apply to the Regional Settlement Commissioner, Khan Market, New 
Delhi, either directly or through a duly appointed agent or through the accredited 
Missions abroad . 

For full details of the procedure to be followed , applicants may refer to the rules 
under the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation ) Act , which have been 
published in the Gazette of India .

No. J/ 4 /55. - The Chief Commissioner, Manipur is pleased to approve the Manipur 
Legal Practitioners Rules, 1955 framed by the Judicial Commissioner, in exercise 
of the powers conferred upon bim by Section 34 of the Manipur State Courts Act, 
1947 as amended by the Manipur State Courts (Amendment) Order , 1950 regarding 
the enrolment of Advocates, Pleaders, Mukhtars and recogoised clerks. 


A. K. Puay , 
Chief Secretary to the Govt . of Manipur. 


In exercise of the powers conferred by section 34 of the Manipur State Courts 
Act 1947 as amended by the Minipur State Courts (Amendment) order 1950 , the 
Judicial Commissioner, Manipur is pleased to make the fullowing Rules for enrolment 
of Advocates, Pleaders , Mukhtars and recognised clerks and with the previons approval 
of the Chief Commissioner, Manipur they are hareby published for the general 
information . : 

CHAPTER I. 

Introductory . 
]. These rules shall be called the Manipur Legal Practitioners Rules 1955 . 
2. They shall come into force at once . 
3. In these rules unless the context shown otherwise 

**Court” means the court of the Judicial Commissioner for Manipur. 
“ Registrar" means the Registrar of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner , 
Manipur . 
“ Advocate " means a person entitled to plead and act before the Court 
of the Judicial Commissioner and before all other courts in Manipur . 
* Pleader” means al person entitled to plea 1 and act before all Courts 
in Manipur except the Court of the Judicial Commissioner. 
“ Mukhtar” means a person entitled to plead and act in any Subordinate 
Criminal Courts or Revenue Office or to practice as Mukhtar in any 
Subordinate Courts . 
Recognised Clerk ” means & clerk other than an articled clerk , employed 
by an Advocate or Pleader and registered under the rules. 
“ Prescribed ” means prescribed by rules, orders or directions issued by 
or under the order of the Judicial Commissioner. 


CHAP I ER II . 

Section A. 
Qualifications and Admission of Advocates . 
1. Any graduate in Law of any University established by law in India , who 
is ) a graduate in Arts, Science, or Cominerce of any such University and who in 
each case has further undergone è course of training under the rules made by the 
Judicial Commissioner in this behalf may present an application for admission to 
the Roll of Advocate of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner for Manipur. 

Provided), firstly , that no woman shall be disqualified for admission to be an 
Advocate by reason only of her sex . 

Provided , secondly , that a person entitled to practice in the Court of Judicial 
Commissioner lofore the enforcoment of this rule shall be allowed to be admitted 
to the Roll of Advocate on presenting an application before the expiry of the 
present terms of his sadad and on compliance of the condition laid down in rule 
4 below . 

Provided , thirdly , thai a Plcader who is not o : berwise qualified to ba enrolled 
as an Advocate , may be so enrolled if he hus practice 1 as a pleader for a period 
of not less than 12 years with ability and repute.

the Advocate by whom he is employed and a coluinn for romarks. 

3. The application for registration of a recognised clerk shall be made to the 
Registrar with a stamped paper of Rs. 2 / - only. The application shall be accom 
panied by it certificate of the advocate or pleader by whom he will be employed , 
that the applicant is to the best of his belief, fit to be employed and will be 
employed bouafide in his own service and for purpose of his legal business . 

4 . The Registrar on receipt of the application make such enquiry as he thinks 
necessary and shall, on being satisfied that the applicant is a fit and proper per 
son to be employed as a recognised 
recognised clerk , enter his 

in the register of 
recognised clerk and shall issue to him a registration card as mentioned in Rulo 
I above. 

5. No advocates clerk shall be allowed to do any work in the court unless 
he has been registered under these rules. Not more than two clerks shall be 
gistered at one time for any advocat , of pleader . 

6 . A person suffering from any contagious or infectious disease or who has 
been convicted of any offence involving moral turpitude or is an undischarged in 
solvent or has ever been declared a tout under the provisions of the Legal Practitioners 
Act 1879 , shall not be registered as a recognised clerk , 

7. A registered clerk shall not make any motion or advance an argument in 
court . He inay act in matters of a routine nature which do not require the personal 
attendance of the advocate and may do the following acts, namely - 

(1 ) receiving notice on bebalf of his employer ; 
(2 ) presenting an appeal or application before the Reader of the court or 

the Registrar ; 
(3 ) obtaining office report on an application for adjournment ;

PRESS NOTIFICATION . 
Whoreas it appears to the Government of Madras that the Tamil book entitled 
‘KANAK KALAI Part I written by Shri V. Bajarun , printed at Thani Nadu Press, 
Madras -2 and published by Ranjithm Pathippagain , Madras – 17 , contains e -po 
cially at pages 10-13 and 20-21, objectionable matter within the meaning of clauso 
( vi ) of section 3 of the l’ress (Objectionable Matter) Act, 1951 (Ceutral Act LVI 
of 1951), being matter which is grossly obscene : 

And whereas the Advi cate General of Madras has granted a certificate under 
Section 11 of the said Act that tho said book contains objec : ionable matter within 
the meauing of section 3 of tbe said Act ; 

Now , therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by section 11 of the said 
Act , the Governor of Madras hereliy declares that all copies , wherever found , of 
the aforesaid look and all other documints containing ropies , reprints , translations 
of, or extracts from the said book shall be forfeited to the Coveramerit on the 
ground specified in the first paragraph of this notification . 

( By order of the Governor)

NOTIFICATION . 


Delhi, the 27th July , 1955 . 
No. F.87 /55 -C. - WHEREAS the Chief Commissioner , Delhi is satisfied that the 
book entitled “ RAMA RETOLD) " in English by Aubrey Memen , published by Chatto 
and Windus Ltd., London , and Clarke , Irwin & Co. Ltd., Torontı ), and printed by 
Butler and Tanner Ltd., Frome and London , in United Kingdom , contains matter 
which is deliberately and maliciously intended to outrage the religious feelings of 
the Hindus by insulting their religious beliefs and the publication of which is 
punishable under section 29 :-A of the Indian Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860 ) ; 


2 


MANIPUR GAZETTE , AUGUST 10 , 1955 . 


NOW , TAEREFORE , on the above- stated grounds and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by section 99 - A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Act V of 1898 ), 
the Chief Commissioner, Delhi hereby declares to be forfieted to Government every 
copy of the said book and all other documents containing copies reprints and 
translations of or extracts from the said book . 

By order, 
Sd / - J. N. Goyal, 
Home Secretary to Government, 

Delhi State, Lelbi. 


Inuphal, the 5th August, 1955 . 
No. A -PWI& W /21 /55 . --The following Resolutions No. 24 (2)/54. Adm dated 
13-10-56 and No. 24 (2 ) /54-Adm.I dated 9-5-55 received from the Government of 
Iodia , Ministry of Irrigation and Power, New Delbi are published for general 
information , 

T. Kipgon , 
Secretary to the Govt. of Manipur. 


No. 2+( 2 )/ 54 - Adm . In view of the importance of expedition and economy in 
the execution of river valley projects, the Government of India have arranged to 
hold Engineers Seminars periodically to enable the heads of major projects to make 
suggestions for improving the methods of work and efliciency and exchange views 
on technical and administrative matters common to these projects and take, wherever 
necessary , co -ordinated action . To derive the maximum benefit from suggestions 
designed to ensure economy and expedition it is important that there should be 
no avoidable delay in taking follow up action . This can not be done unless deci 
sions are taken quickly at the highest level and the suggestions implemented both 
by the Central and the State Governnients . The Government of India have , there 
fore, set up , in consultation with the State Governments concerned , " the Co -ordi 
nation Committee of Engineers ” and “ the Co - ordination Board of Ministers” . The 
composition of the Committee and the Board is as follows : 


Co-ordination Committee or Engineers : 


l . Chairman , Central Water and Power Commission . 
2. Deputy Secretary , Ministry of Irrigation and Power. 
3. Chief of Natural Resources , Planning Commission . etc. , etc. 


Chairman . 
Meinber , 
Member 


Co - ordination Board of Ministers :

or 


1. Candidates for the award of Scholarships shall be members of the Scheduled 
Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes as recognised for the purpose , 
shall be citizens of India including Jammu & Kasbmir or Sikkim and sball have 
passed the Matriculation Examination of a University established by law in India 

any other equivalent examination of & recognised University or Board of 
Secondary Education in India or in a foreign country . 

2. Each applicant for Scholarship should send a certificate signed by a Member 
of the Parliament/Member of State Legislalure/Municipal Commissioner/Member of 
the District Board /Gazetted Officer stating that he/ she belongs to Scheduled Castes / 
Scheduled Tribes/Other Backward ( lasses, and is a citizen of India . 

3. The Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes Scho 
larships Board , hereinafter called " the Board ” may Subject to

No. 1 intending to pursue studies in recognised Institutions in India in the follow 
ing courses mentioned in order of preference .

13. A Government of India scholarship -holder will not hold any other scholar 
ship except a merit scholarship from University or Board or from the State Government 
or & grant for purchase of text books from any source ; but if awarded State 
Government or any other scholarship of higher value not based on merit, he / she 
will have the option to avail of that scholarship after refunding the entire amount 
of the Central Scholarship drawn during the year . In cases where the value of 
Central Scholarship is less than that of State Scholarship , the State Government 
may , if they so desire , supplement the Contral Scholarship of a particular scholar 
by raising it to the level of the State Scholarship

14. The scholarship shall ordinarily be tenably for a period not exceeding one 
academic year it may be renewed at the discretion of the Board subject to funds 
being available for a period not exceeding one academic year at a time to enable 
the holder to complete an approved course of study . 

15. If a scholar fails to pass the annual examination for the course of study 
for which scholarship is awarded in a year , the scholarship will automatically cease 
and his scholarship will ordinarily be renewed . He may , however , apply for a fresh 
scholarship again after passing the annual examination in future year. If a scholar 
is unable to appear in the annual examination owing to illness , he should inforın 
the Board accordingly before the examination is over through the Ilead of the 
Institution with a medical certificate from it registered medical practitioner ; failing 
which his application for renewal of scholarship will not be considered . The application 
for renewal will be considered only if the Head of the Institution , on the basis of 
perfornuance , certifies that the candidate was likely to pass if he had taken the 
Examination . 

16. A scholarship sl.all be cancelled if the scholar changes the subject of course 
for which the scholarship was originally awarded or changes the Institution of study , 
WITHOUT THE PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE BOARD . The Heads of 

Institu 
tions shall report such cases to the Boud and stop payment of scholarship money. 
The amount already paid niay also be recovered at the discretion of the Board . 

17 A scholar is liable to refund the schularship amount at the discretion of 
the Board if bo discontinues his studies during the courso of the year for which 
a scholarship is awarded . 

18. Every scholar shall submit to the Board a statement at the end of each 
term from tho Ilead of the lustitution in regard to bis progress and general conduct . 
If it should appear at any time that scholar has by reason of his own 
default failed to make satisfactory progress or has been guilty of misconduct such 
as resorting to or participating in strikes , irregularity in attendance without permis 
sion of the authorities concernel etc., the Board may either cancel the scholarship 
or stop or withbold further payment for such period as they may think fit . 

19. The scholarship moneys shall be paid in two half yearly instalments by means of 
a Remittance Transfer Receipt drawn in the nearest branch of the Imperial Bank of India 
or the nearest Government Treasury /Sub - Treasury , in favour of the Head of the Institu 
tion in which the scholar is enrolled . It is also the responsibility of the scholar to see that 
the receipt signed by him for the payment received in each instalment is forwarded 
through the Head of the Institution to the Board as soon us the period covered 
by each instalment is over , otherwise the payment of the 2nd instalıuent will be 
delayed . Payments are not ordinarily made by Postal Order but if made in this 
manner in any exceptional case , the Postal con mission shall be deducted out of 
the scholarship amount .

ইম্ফালদা নেশনেল তােলুনটিয়ার ফোর্শ কেশ 


ইক্ষাল , তাং ২৮।৭।৫৫ ইং জুলাই । 
মনিপুরদা নেশনেল ভােলুটিয়ার কেম্প তাং ১৫ সেপ্তেম্বৱদগী খুলিগনি হুনা তাং ১৪ 

ওক্টোবর ১৯৫৫ দ 
লােগনি । নেশনেল ভােলন্টিয়াব ফোশ হায়বা অসি লানগীদমক্তা লৈবাক কিনবা নত্তে, মসিগী মরু ওইবা খলদি 
দেশ বাশি খুদিংমক জাতিসী ওইনা খাবা কনবা , লমচৎ ব্যবহার ফজবা অমসুং দেশগ সেবাদা পুকিং চংবা তমনননি । 

মুমিৎ ৩০ নিগ ট্রেনিং অসি, চহি ৫ গী মনুংদা মী লাখ মঙাদা পীগনি , ভারতকী মফম খুদিংমা মে ১ লাদগী 
কেম্প ২০০ লিংদুনা মী লাখ অমা ট্রেনিং গদবনি । ট্রেনিং টিম খুদিংমক কেপতেন অমনা ওফিসার কমান্ডিং 
ওইগনি । 

“ ত্রেনিং চংবা রাবা - দৰা অমসুংরেনি অমনতৌগদ মরমশিং 
চহি ১৮ দগী ৪০ ফাওবগী মনুদা লৈবা মশা ফবা ভারতকী নাগরিক খুদিংমক চংবা য়াগনি । 

সিফাই খল্প 
অমসুং এন, সি , সি , কেডেত ওইরিবশিদি য়াওবা বােই । 

মশানা য়ানা ট্রেনিং তৌগদৌরিবা মী খুদিংমক অরেপ্পা নাইদনা সুমিৎ ৩০ নিগী ট্রেনিং মপু ফানা য়াওগদবনি , ট্রেনিংদা 
লৈরিঙৈদা করি মিলিটারি এক্ত অমতগ মখাপােন নত্তে, লােইরগশু মিলিটারি সাভিশ চংগদলনি হায় করি 
অমত লৈতে । 

ট্রেনিশিংনা ট্রেনিংদা লৈরিঙৈদা শােক- পন , লাইনা পকলকপা অমসুং শিবা থােকলবদি সরকাবনা মাগী দায়ি 
লৌদুনা পেলন নগা করিগুম্বা মখলগী ক্ষতি পুরন পীবােই । 

কনাগু ট্রেনি অমবু , মবম চানা , কেম্পতগী তাহােকপা , মাগী পােকেট এলায়েন্স ককথৎপনচিংবা ওফিশ 
কলিং তৌবা ঙমই । ট্রেনিশিংগীদমক তমুর খনবা কেম্পত লৈফম ফংগনি । 

“ ত্রেনিদা লৈরিঙৈদা ত্রেনিশিঙনা ফংগদবা অমসুং অতৈ অকুপ- অতা ” 
ট্রেনিশিংনা কেম্পতা লৈরিঙৈদা শিজিন্নবা কেম্পকী পােৎ খুদিংমক ট্রেনিং লােইগা অমুক লৌশিনহৌগদবনি । 

রেশন ট্রেনিংদা লৈবিবা মী খুদিংমক ফ্রি বেশন ফংগনি নগা নােমদা ট্রেনি অমগ বেশন এলাওযেঙ্গ ওইনা 
লুপা ১০ ( শিকি মঙ ) ফংগনি । হায়রিবা এলায়েন্স অসি রেশন সপ্লাই তৌবা ঙমত্রবা মতমগীতনি । 

তলৰ অমসুং এলায়েন্সঃ - ট্রেনিং মপুং ফারবা মতুংদা মী অমন নোংমদা মখাই ১ গী ( ০ ) হিংসা 
সুমিৎ ৩০ নিগ লুপা ১৫ পােকেট খচ্চা ফংগনি । 

অৱা পােখামঃ- ট্রেনিং টিম খুদিংগী অৱ -পােথানবগ মরমদা লুপা ৩০০, কাইথোকলি , মাসিনা ট্রেনিশিংগী 
পুকনিং থৌগৎবা অফ মাইকৈদা শেমগৎ শাগপগী ওইনা — পাননবা নুঙাইবা শরিক লাইশু, এমফোন বেকো তাবা , 
ইশৈ -নােমাইগী যন্ত্র খােবা , মখল মখলগী শন্নিবা অসিনচিংবা অসিগ দমক্তা চাদিং তৌগনি ।

DRAFT ANNOUNCEMENT 
The Central Social Welfare Board will consider errly in November applications 
for grants from voluntary institutions for the period November, 1955 to March , 1956 . 
Institutions may send in their applications to this office immediately in any case not 
later than 20th August , 19:15 on the prescribed proforma, copies of which can be 
obtained from this office . The original copy with a copy should be sent to this office 
and another advance copy to the Central Social Welfare Board , 10 --Kitchner Road , 
Diplomatic Enclave, New Delhi. The following conditions may be carefully noted by 
institutions intending to make applications. 

(1) An application will not be considered from any institution , which has already 
received a grant for a period extending upto the 31st March , 1956. 

( 2 ) Applications for starting new institutions in areas now included in a Welfare 
Extension Project will not be considered , except from institutions which have already 
existed in that area before the starting of that project. 

(3) Every institution should give complete information about its management, 
that is , whether it is run by an individual or by a Managing Committee elected 
or non -elected . Full details of existing assets and collections already made by volun 
tary effort shoulıl he furnished . 

(4 ) Every application should give brief details of the scheme for which the 
grant will be untilised , as also the institution s normal expenditure on those items and 
its matching contribution . 

In cases where the scheme is the maintenance of orphanage or a home for destitute 
women , etc., or for the free distribution or milk or medicines, the number of existing 
iomates or beneficiaries and the additional number to be benefitted by grant should 
be clearly indicated . 

(5 ) Branches of all India and regional organisations should be asked to send 
their applications to the Central Office of their organisation . The Central Office of 
the organisation should send the original application with its recommendation to the 
State Board and an advance copy for information to the Central Board , also with 
its recommendation , 
Note : -- The statement of income and expenditure furnished by Branch should 

relate only to its own income and expenditure , and not to the whole orga 
pisation . This applies also in cases where the same institution has a number 

of separate Branches in different places. 

(6 ) Since the grant will be only for a period of 6 six months, institutions should 
frame their estimates for this period only and ask for only so much as they can 
spend by the end of March, 1956. No extention of the period will be granted 
subsequently . 

( 7 ) A request fur à grant for each purpose should indicate the total 
quirements of the institution for the period in question for that purpose and the 
amount which will be met from its own resources . In the case of requests for grants 
for new buildings, it should be indicated whether the institution has legal title to the 
land on wbich the building is proposed to be constructed . Similary, in the case of 
requests for grants for additions or alternations to buildings, it should be clearly indicated 
whether the institution has legal title to the land and existing building .

PRESS NOTE . 
INSTRUCTIONS TO EMPLOYEES TO DECLARE AUGUST 15 

A PAID HOLIDAY. 
In pursuance of instructions issued by the Central Ministry of Labour on pre 
vious anniversaries of Independence Day , Workers were permitted to participate in 
the August 15th celebrations without being made to suffer any loss in wages . 

A similar directive has been issued this year by the Govt . of India to their 
officers in charge of industrial undertakings and thay hope that other employers 
also will co -operate with them by declaring this national day as a paid holiday . 

In view of the great importance of the occasion , Government believe that many 
industrial undertakings have already prescribed August 15th as one of the regular 
holidays but where this has not been done, they hope that the employers will treat 
the day an additional paid holiday and not as a substituted holiday. 


Imphal :-Prated and published by the Suparintendent, Government Prose . O. 200 / 10-8-85.

General of Police , Manipur sanction for 
With reference to your lotter No. HP /97 /52 , dated the 31st 
on the above subject, I am directed to say that the President is plens 3d to redesignate

received from the Registrar, the Institute Chartered Accountants of Iodia , New

T. Kipgen

In pursuance of Regulation 23 of the Chartered Accountants Regulations, 1949, 
the Council of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Indit is pleased to direct 
that the Preliminary Examination under the said Regulations shall be held on the 
17th , 18th , 19th , 2ist and 22nd November 195.), the First Examination on the 
17th , 18th , 19th , 21st, 22nd , 23rd and 24th November , 1955 and the Final Exa 
mination on the 17th 18th , 19th , 21st , 22nd, 23rd and 24th Nov. 1955 . Tbe 
examinations will be held at each of the following centres provided that a sufficient 
number of candidates present themselves for examination : 

( a ) ALLAHABAD , (b ) BOMBAY , (c ) CALCUTTA , ( d ) DELHI, (e ) HYDERABAD 
(Dn ) and ( f ) MADRAS. 

Applications for admission to these examinations are required to be made on the 
prescribed forms, copies of which may be obtained from the Secretary to the Council 
of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India , New Delhi. Each such appli 
cation together with the necessary certificates and a Domand Draft payable at New 
Delhi and drawn in favour of the said Secretary for an examination fee of Rs. 25 / 
in the case of the Preliminary Examination , Rs. 50 : - in the 

of the First 
Examination and Ref . 75 /- for admission to both the Groups or Rs. 50 /- for admis 
sion to one group only of the Final Examination, must be sent so as to reach the 
Secretary to the Council not later than the 19th September 1955 . An additional 
fee of Rs , 50 /- is payable by candidates who apply for the first time for admission 
to the Final Examination and who have been exempted from passing the First 
Examination .

No. J / 17 /55 . —The following notification issued by the Central Government under 
Section 12 of the Commissions of Inquiry Act , 1952 is published for general infor 
mation : 

No. 16 / 1 /55 - Judicial (1 ) 

Government of Iudia 
Ministry of Home Affairs . 

NOTIFICATION . 

New Delhi- 2 , the 26th July , 1955 . 
In exercise of the powers conferred by section 12 of the Commissions of Inquiry 
Act , 1952 (LX of 1952), the Central Government hereby makes the following rules 
for the issue and service of summons loy & Commission of Inquiry appointed by 
that Government, namely : -- 

Rules. 
1. The Commission may issue summons to persons whose attendance is 

required either to give evidence or to produce documents. 
2 . Every summons issued by the Commission shall be in duplicate and 

signed by the Chairman or such person as he empowers in this behalf 
and sealed with the seal of the Commission ; and it shall specify the 
time and place at which the person siimmoned is required to attend 
and also whether his attendance is required for the purpose of giving 

evidence or to produce a document , or for both purposes. 
3. A person may be summoned to produce a document, without being 

summoned to give evidence ; and any person summoned merely to produce 
& document shall be deemed to have complied with the summons if 
he causes such document to be produced instead of attending personally 

to produce the sanie . 
4. A summons to produce documents may be for the production of certain 

specified documents or for the production of all doouments of a certain 

description in the possession or power of the person summoned . 
5 . Every summons shall be served by sending it by post to the person 

for whom it is intended or in such other manner as the Commission 

may direot . 
6. The provisions of the foregoing rules shall apply , as far as may be, to 

every other process issued by the Commission . 


A. K. Ray , 
Chief Secretary to the Govt . of Manipur .

No. J /17 ;55 . -The following notification issued by the CentralGovernment under 
Section 12 of the Commissions of Inquiry Act , 1952 is published for general infor 
mation : 

No. 16 / 1 /55 - Judicial ( 1 ) 

Government of India 
Ministry of Home Affairs. 

NOTIFICATION . 

New Delhi- 2 , the 26th July , 1955 . 
In exercise of the powers conferred by section 12 of the Comidissions of Inquiry 
Act, 1952 (LX of 1952 ), the Central Government hereby makes the following rules 
for the issue and service of summons by a Commission of Inquiry appointed by 
that Government , namely : 

Rule s . 
1. The Commission may issue summons to persons whose attendance is 

required either to give evidence or to produce documents. 
2. Every summons issued by the Commission shall be in duplicate and 

signed by the Chairman or such person as he en powers in this behalf 
and scaled with the goal of the Commission ; and it shall specify the 
time and place at 

which the person summoned is required to attend 
and also whether his attendance is required for the purpose of giving 

evidence or to produced document, or for both purposes. 
3. A person may be summoned to produce a document, without being 

summoned to give evidence ; and any person summoned merely to produce 
& docunient shall be deemed to have complied with the summons if 
he causes such document to be produced instead of attending personally 

to produce the sane. 
4 . A summons to produce documents may be for the production of certain 

specified documents or for the pruduction of all documents of a certain 

description in the possession or power of the person summoned . 
5. Every summons shall be served by sending

SINHASTI FAIR will be held at Visik and Trimbak in Bombay State fourteen

Bairagis, Gosavis etc., from verious parts of India will attend the Fair and they 
are likely to curry with them , intoxicants such as Bhans , Ganja Charns, Cocaine ,

an offence under the Bombay Prohibition Act, 1949 . Persons found to be in 
possession of such articles are liable to be prosecuted under the law in force in 
Bombay Stato .

NOTIFICATION . 


Dated Shillong , the 5th September , 1955 . 


Suluject : - Veritication by the Treasury Officer of countersignature on the Travel 

ling allowance claim of Gazetted Government servant for the period 

prior to his transfer to the payment of a new Treasury Officer . 
No. TM./4/55/26.-A reference is invited to rule 177 of the Central Treasury 
Rule Vol-l, which inter-alia imposes an obligation on the Troasury Officer to verify 
the venuineness of the countersignature of the Controlling Officer on the Travel 
ling allowance claims of a gazetted Officer s bill. A question has been raised as to 
how & Treasury Officer is to satisfy 

Officer is to satisfy himself of the genuineness of the counter 
signature of the Controlling Officer in respect of a claim prior to the transfer of 
the officer to his payment . As the matter stands at present, no provision exists in 
the Trcasury Rules providing for thu action to be taken by the now Treasury 
Onicer in this regard . To meet this lacuna in the rules, it has been decided that 
all the controlling Officers empowered to countersign bills should send their speci 
men signatures to all the Treasury Oflicers duly attested by the Treasury Officer 
of the district, in which they draw bills so thilt the new Treasury Officer nay 
not have any difficulty to verify the counterzignatura . 

The Controlling Officers (Central) and all the Treasury and Sul - Tresury Officers 
in Assam , Tripura and Manipur will please see that the procelure detailed above 
in this regard is strictly followed . 


Amitabha Ghoshi , 
Deputy Accountant General (II), A : 84m .

NOTIFICATION. 

Dated Shillong, the 8th August , 1955 . 
Subject :-Acceptance of remittances of Excise Duty on despatches of coal/coke 

by means other than rail. 
TM.2 / 10 /54 / 24.- In continuation of this offich notification No. TM.2/10/57/77 dated 
the 14th February 55 it is hereby notified for the information and guidance of 
all Treasury Officers & Sub - Treasury Officers in Assam , Manipur and Tripura that 
copies of chalan relating to deposits under the head " I Union Excise - Excise Duty 
on Coal & Coke (a ) Levied under the ( oa ! Mines ( conservation and safety) Act, 1952" 
nend not ba sent to the Collector of Central Excise . The procedure to be followed 
in such cases is as follows : 

Every owner of Colliery intending to make payment on account of excise duty 
on despatches of coal/coke by means other than rail shall present the same along 
with a chalan in triplicate. The Treasury Officer shall return two copies of the 
chalan to the depositor who shall keep ono copy for himself and transmit the other 
copy to the Chairman , Coal Board , Calcuttil, who is responsible for the assessment 
and realisation of such duty . 

S. S. Lal, 
Deputy Accountant General (I) , Assam .

PUBLIC NOTICE NO . 48 ITC (PN )/ 55 . 

Now Delhi, the 24th August, 1955 . 
Subject :-Import of Films niade from transparent cellulose or Viscacella , Royasine, 

Transparent cellulose wrapping and other transparent paper (Sr. No. 122 ( vii)/V . 
Attention of the importers is invited to remark (ii) against Sr. No. 122 ( vii)/ V 
in Section II of the current Red Book , from which it will be seen that quota 
licences are subject to & condition that imports to the extent of balf the value 
thereof should be completed within three months of the date of issue . 

2. Certain representations have been made that this condition operates to the 
hardship of Established Importers holding sinall value quota licences. The matter has 
been considered and it has been decided that qucta licences issued ty Established 
Importers upto a value of Rs. 1,000/- will be exempt from the operation of the 
condition mentioned iu remark (ii) against S. No. 122( 111)/V in Section II of the 
current Red Book . It will thus be open to Established Importers with quota 
licences upto Rs. 1,000 /- to effect imports against such licences at any time within 
the period of validity of the liconces. 

3. This concession will also be applicable to licences for this item for a value 
upto Rs. 1,000/- which may have been issued during the earlier licensing period / 
periods and which may still be current. 

4. No formal amendment of the cɔndition , if endorsed on such licences, would 
be necessary . 

S. N. Bilgrami,

and to receive applications with respect to the verified land claims.

written in bold red ink " Land Claim application only ” .

No. 1 /51/54.F. — Whereas the Film Advisory Board has been functioning for recom 
mending documentaries and newsreels produced by the Films Division and by private

the cinema licences and whereas a direction hils now been issued by the lintral Govern 
ment under sub -section ( 4 ) of section 12 of the Cinematograph Ac !, 9.). (XXXVII of 
1952), and by the various Stat, Governmen s under their own Arts , it has b on i cided 
that the Film Advisory Board should be entrusted with the res;:03: ibility ofapproving 
films which may be regarded as scie : it : fic film-, films intended for -ducational purposes , 
films dealing with news and curr lit events or documentary films with reference to these 
directions.

( 2 ) Memburs other than the ex -officio members and the member of the Advisory 
Panel of the Central Board of Film Censors , Bombay , shall bh appointed for a period of 
two years and will be eligible for re -appointment. The member of the Advisory Panel 
shall be appointeil as a member of the Board for the full term of his membership of the 
Panel. 


( 3) The Guvernment of India may for a cause sufficient in its opinion , remove any 
member of the Board before the expiration of the period of bis office. 


(4 ) Tbe non - official members of the Board will work in an honorary capacity . They 
may be paid such compensatory allowance as the Central Government may from time 
to time determine . 


(5 ) The Regional Officer of the Central Board of Film Censors at Bombay will be 
the Secretary of the Board . 


(6 ) No act or proceeding of the Board shall be called in question on the ground 
merely of the existence of any Vacancy in or defect in the constitution of the Board . 


(7 ) Unlesy otherwise directed by the Government of India , the Headquarters of the 
Board shall be ut Bombay . 


(8 ) Meetings of the Board shall be presided over by the Chairman , and , in his 
absence the members present may elect one among themselves to preside . 


( 9) The quorum of the Board shall be three . 


(10 ) The decision of the Board shall be that of the majority of the inembers attend 
ing the meeting and in the event of an equality of votes , the presiding officer shall 
have a second or casting voti . The decision of the Board shall be firal. If any appli 
cant wants to make any representation in regard to the film submitted by bim , however , 
the Board shall give him an opportunity to do so and it shall be open to the Brard 
to revise their decision in the light of any such representation . 

(11) The Board shall be ordinarily meet every week for the purpose of approving

( 12 ) Any person , firm , organisation or Government desirous of having any of his

(b) the surcharge payable shall in no case exceed half the amount by which the tota ! 

income ( before reduction of the saill allowance, if any , for earned income ) exceeds 

the said limit 
(b ) The allowance for " arned income" on incomes upto Rs . 25,000 /- is one -fifth of such 
earned incomr, subject to a maximum of Rs. 4,0 10) . In the case of curned income exceeding

one fifth of the annount by which thu carned income exceeds ts . 25,000 /- . 

(c) The rebate of income tax on account of life insurance premia , provident fund contri

Imphul, the 26th September , 1955 . 
With effect from the 28th September, 1953, a daily courier service from Imphal 
to Tamenglong and vice versa will be set up to cirry mails between these two hoad 
quarters . Lamboos of the Deputy Commissioner s establishment will work as couriers . 
The couricr service will be open to utilisation by all Government Departments in 
Imphal as well as in Tamenglong . All inails intended for delivery to the $ . D. O., 
Tamenglɔng or other Ollicers posted there should be liandud over to the Deputy Commis 
sioner s Office and those to be despatched from Tainenglong to Imphal by Officers 
there should be delivered to the Office of the S.D.O., Tamenglony for onward trans 
mission to the respective destinations. Mails should be handed over to the offices 
inentioned during office hours on working days and at 15 A.M. on holidays . 

Denartments concerned will please direct their messengers to the respective offices 
at Imphal and at Tamenglong every day to collect their mails . 
This arrangement will continue until further orders.

NO TIFICATION . 

Dated Shillong, the 1st October, 1955 . 
No. TM / 10 /55 / 31. - It is notified for informition and guidance of all Treasury 
Officers and Sul - Treasury Officers in Assam , Tripura and Manipur that the remitters 
applications relative to drawings effected by the Treasu ies and Sub - Treasurits do not in 
most cases contain the serial numlier and the actual dato of issue of drafts . The absence 
of these essential part.culars in the applications makes their identification with the relative 
paid drafts very difficult on the part of the Reserve Bank of India , Central Accounts 
Suction , Calcutta . Consequently it gives rise to avoidable correspondence with the Drawing 
Officers. It is therefore , requested that all necessary particulars should invariably be 
furnished in the applications in the space provided fur in the relative forms to avoid 
the difficulties so long experienced ly the Reserve Bank of India . 

S. S. Lal, 
Daputy Accountant General ( 1), Assam .
