HINTS ON DETECTING COUNTERFEITS OF PURE NICKEL COINS. 
With the introduction of Pure Nickel series of coins in 1946 , comprisiog Rupeos , 1/2 
Rupees and 1/4 Rupees, the design of the- e coins was changed ; the sizes and standard 
weights of the coins remaining the sume its in previous issues , except in the case of the 
Rupee, which became smaller in diameter and consequently thicker, the weight re 
maining the same at 180 grains troy- the 1/2 Rupees and !/4 Rupees weighting 90 grains 
and 45 grains respectively . I ure Nickel rupees were first issued bearing the dat : 1947 
and 1/2 Rupees and 1! 4 Rupees bearing the dala 1948 Pure Nickel ruparon of 1947 
and 1/2 rupees and 1/4 rupees vf 1946 aud 1917 bors on their Reverse the Tiger and on 
the Obverse the elligy of King George VI. No coins bearing the date 1948 and 194 !) were 
minted and issued by the Indian Mints. Pure Nickel Rupees, 1/2 Rupees and 1/4 Rupees 
of 1950 and op -wards lear on their obverse thy Asoka Pillar and on the 
the Ears of coin design . In the Pure Nickel series of coins the rupees are security 
edged , whilst the 1/2 and 1/4 rupees bear it plain willing. 

Adoption of Pure Nickel in itself is a safeguard against counterfeiting . One 
of the Chief advantage lies in the difficulties of production . Pure Nickel cannot 
readily be used for the making of small sand castings having a good surface 
finish . As the chief method of the Counterfeiter is to individual coins 
in sand or metal moulds , he must employ some alternative medium which con 
readily be detected . A distinctive fouture of nickel is that it is magnetic , 

magaetic , and 
no other metal which might conceivably be considered suitable for coinage has 
this property . Therefore a magnet can be used as a test of the genuinenest of 
pure nickel coins. Further more pire mickel is particularly free from tarnishing , 
any dirt or finger marks can be wiped clean with a dry rag . 

Two kinds of counterfeits of pure nickel coins are found viz . cast and struck , 
or a combination of the two . 

Cast counterfeits are the most easily made , and therefore are more usually 
found . The mould into which the molten 

tbe nolten metal is poured , may be made of 
Band, clay , powdered burnt brick , plaster of paris or similar materials and the 
impression on the mould is taken from a genuino coin . The mould has a small 
hole or gate out in the rim , throngh which the molten metal is poured . The 
metal which fills this hole , and solidifies with the rest of the casting , forms a 
projection on the rim of the cast coin , which must be cut off to enable the 
rim at this point to be finished and milled by hand , and the security groove put in . 
Signs of this land finishing can usually be detected on the rim of cast counterfeits . 


Cast 


MANIPUR GAZETTE , OCTOBER 29 , 1955 . 


3 


are 


Struck counterfeits made by striking or pressiny blanks Witween dies of 
hard metal, thy designs of which are engraved by hand, or from dies of softer 
metal on which the impressions can be transferred from a genuine coin . The blanks, 
thus struck , may have been tirst caat or cut from sheet metal. 

Counterl.it : ara more easily detected if comprired with one or more genuine 
coins of the same design , using a magnifying glass if necessary . A suspicious coid 
muy also be weighed against a gonuine coin showing the same amount of wear, 
since most counterfeits which do not contain much lead are lighter than genuine 
coins. 

The only disadvantage of pure nickel coins is that they have no ring , and 
for centuries lydians have been accus omed to judge the genuineness of the silver 
coins by listening for the clear ring of high touch silver coins. There is no doubt 
that the ringing test diminished in importance when quaternary alloy coins with 
50 % silver were introduced . These coins give a much higher and sharper ring than 
their bigh touch predecessors . The cumbness of pure nickel coins however is com 
pressed fur by their magnetic properties and any small boy equipped with a cheap 
magnet can easily distinguish a chunter feit from it genuine coin . 

The thickness of it genuine coin is uniform whilst counterfeits are sometimes 
thicker at one side than at the other , and are often slightly bent or distorted . 
80 that they will not lie evenly between two other coins . 

The rim of genuina pure nickel Rupels, 1 / Rupees and 1/4 Rupees are 
regularly miled and all round with straight indentutions at right angles to the faces, 
but pure nickel rupees have also a security devise in the cense of he willed edge. 
This device consists of a shallow gruore with il design consisting of a chain of 
small beads in relief in two sections separated by blank spaces In counterfeits of 
these cuins the willing is often at a slant, the spaces between the indentations 
irregular and the indentations themselves uneven or broken . The milling can best 
be examined by placing the suspected coin between two yood coins of the some 
description , when defects can roadily be detected . 

Coins should not be classed is counterfeits solely on account of bad mil 
ling , since genuine coins are found with worn milling , with portions soldered for 
use as ornaments or with the edges filled or touched up . Coins of which the milling 
is good however, are seldom counterfeits . 

The heads which appear in relief, insiile the security groove on the Rupee 
coins, should be clear cut, well defined , and uniform in size and shape. The blank 
portions of the groove should be equal in length . In counterfeits , the beads are often 
badly shaped and uneven in size , the intervening spaces boing sometimes filled with 
metal. The blank portions usually shown signs of metal having been scooped out 
by hand , resulting the bruken willing on either side of the blank portion , and 
possibly & wider groove in genuine coins.

I RESS NOTE , 


Certain difficulties have been experience 1 liy the Silk Trade in India regarding 
the clearance of their consignments of Tassar Silk Fabrics , exported to foreign countries, 
at the destination in the alısence of a Certificate about the origin and contents of 
goods exported . In order to oviate these difficulties, it has been decided to introduce, 
with iminediate effect, a procedure of certification by the Govt. of India . The procedure 
will be as follows. The exporters of Silk l abrics in General and Tassar Silk Fabrics 
in particular will, in their own interest , forward to the Secretary, Central Silk Board , 
office of the Textile Commissioner , Haraw sla Building , Wittet Road , Ballard Estate , 
Bombay - 1, the samples of silk goods that they desire to export to foreign countries 
with necessary details. The samples will be oxamined by the Board and its seal 
affixed on thom certifying the origin and contents of such samplos and then returned 
to the Parties concerned to effect exports .

PRESS NOTE . 
DELIVERY OF BOOKS TO PUBLIC LIBRARIES 
The Government of India have declared the Central Libury, Town Hall , Bonday , 
as one of the public litr irina llodor the Delivery of Books (Public Librari s ) Act, 195.1 . 

The Act provides for the free and compulsory supply of one copy of all books 
published in India tu th National Library , clealta :ud to cach of three public 
lilvraries so declared liy the Government of India . 

Someti 110 ago the Connermura Public Library , Madras way declared as a " Public 
Library." The present nutification brin ys the number of " Public Libraries " to two , 
excluding thy National Library , Calcutta . The third * Public Library ” has yet to be 
specified . 

Tbc ( entral Government desire to draw the attention of all publisbers of books 
in India that under the said Act , failure to sup :: ly the books to the National Li 
brary , Calcutta , Connemara Public Library , Madras, and the Central Library , Town 
llall , Bombay , will be an offence under the Act . 

The object of the Act was to securis for the country four libraries in four diffe 
rent parts of the country , wbich , by stocking all buohy published in India , will act, 
as Centres for the promotion of kuowledge and research .

EJRLY PJYMENT OF COMPENSATION TO WIDOWS. 
In a Press Note ditoj July 29 , 1953 it was announced that widows baving verified 
claims in tbeir own names etc. would be paid cash upto a masivum of Rs. 8,000 /- and 
would be given priority in the matter of payment. 

This concession is now being extended to those who became widows subsequent to the 
filing of compensation applicatious loy their busbands. 

Such widows , whether or not their applications were made in their own names , will 
be given priority in the matter of the payment of compensation . 


EXPLOITATION OF SMALL DISPLACED CLAIMANTS . 
GOVERNMENT NOT TO RECOGNISE SALE AND PURCHASE OF CLAIMS . 

PAYMENT OF COMPEXSATION TO BE EXTENDED . 
The Government of India have noticed with some concern that the concession which 
Was given to displaced persons with claims who wished to purchase property in the 
Com ensation pool, to associate other claimants with them to make up the amount of their 
bid , is being abused . 

Some persons interested in the purchase of pool property have bien including those 
cluimants who are in need of ready cash to part with their claims at prices far below the 
amount of compensation payable on such claims. The oliject of the Government in per 
mitting claimants to assccirte among themselves for the purpose of buying property was 
to facilitate both the purch - se and the salo of such property and to enable genuine buyers 
to purchase property against claims. 

To put an end to exploitation , the Government has decided not to recoynise sale and 
purchase of claimy. 

Such sale ai d purchase of claims will not be recognised . Jlowever, if oluimants wish 
to combine to purchase property, they would be permitted to do so , but th : sale certificate 
will be made out in the name of all these persons and their shares specified in it according 
to the amount contributed by each of them either by adjustment of claim or by cash . 

To give imn diate relief to sm : ll claimants. orders have already issued that thoso 
claimants wh:0 : e clainis are for Rs. 2,000 or less should be given priority for payment in 
cash . 

Cash payments upto Rs. 8,000 will continue to be made to claimants halonging to 
needy categories , such it widows , grantees of maintenance allowance and displaced 
claimants who are suffering from T.B. or cancer or whose dependants : ire suffering from 
these diseases , minors, inmates of Homes , receipients of cash doles , etc. 

The range of persons to whom early relief should be given by paymont of compen 
sation in oash is being further extended . 

Instructions have been issued that claimants whose verified claims do not exceed 
Rs. 10,000 and who are to be paid in cash should have their casez dealth with 
expeditiously

নােলিশ । 


নং STOil/ 65ং১১২১৫৫ । 
এজা পুমা খঙহঞ্জরি মাদুদি মণিপুর গভর্ণমেণ্টক প্রেস নােট নং ১০ তাং ২১০৫৫ইংগী মতুং ইয়া চলি 
ডিসেম্বর থাগী তাং ১৫ দগী হোন। ষ্টেট ট্রেডিং আফিসনা পয়লা নম্বরগী চেং লৌউবাশিংগী ইম্ফালদা লৈ হৌগলি । 
চেংগী মমলদি বােড়। য়াওনা মনদা সুপা ৯ (মাপল) নি । হৱ ভাড়া , গাড়ীদগী থাংখা, ওনবা অমসুং গুদামা এ 
দিনবগী ( ষ্টো তৌবগী) খরচ চেং তীবা মীনা পগবনি । বােড়াদি অহন ওইগদৰনি অসুং বােড়। এ যে 
নি অনিমখাই হাপদবনি । চেং তন্মৰিবা মী খুদিংমা “ লৌউৰা মীনি অমসুং ভরি চেং অদু মশা মশানা উবা 
সৌদী থােকপা চেনি হয়না অই চে অষা (ডিক্লারেসন অমা ) গুনগী থাবা বা স্বাক্ষী অলি আওনা সহী 
তৌছু পৰিগৰনি । 

ষ্টেট ট্রেডিং অফিসনা সৌগদৰা চেংগ নমুনা (সেম্পল) আফিতা খমজরে । চেং তীগেহাবা লৌউবা মী খৈন। 
আফিতা লানা সেম্পল য়েংবিরগদৰনি । কনাগুম্বা মীনা সেম্পলদগী তানা চেং পুবিরকলবদি চেং সৌজরােই (বিজেক্ট 
তেজগনি ) । 

টে ; লৌৰা মরেদি কৈধেলগী ওইনা মখাদা পীরিবা তারিখ অমসুং মনশিংগী মতুংইয়া বাজার বাজার কোকি 
খুলশি লৈবা লৌউবাশিংদগী অমুক পুং ১০ দগ মুংথিল পুং অনি ফাওৰা লেজগনি । নােংমদা পৰি পৰিা বাজারশিপ 
মনশিং অদুগা হেমা পুবিরপা অদুগ দায়ী অফিসনা পুজরােই, অহেনবা চেং মখৈ লৌসুবোই । 

চেং সীগদ 
মশিন। ষ্টেট ট্রেজি অফিসক কামাে : বাংমদ । অকোন অহন নাইন। লেংদুনা লৈৰিগদবনি । 
মনু মুৰ সৌরমদাইদা অঙ্গা নােটিশ অম অমুক তেমনি।

PRESS NOTE . 


Indphal, the 26th December , 1955. 
" Indian Women s Eduontion Association " 

London Scholarship . 
The Indian Women s Education Association , London has offered one scholarship 
for the year 1956-57 to an Indian Woman Graduate for studies in the United Kinga 
dom in Education , including Physical Education , 

The scholarship is tenable for one year and is of the value of £ 300 . In addi 
tion passage expenses both . ways upto £ 150 and academic fees will be borne by the 
Association . The candidates must not be more than 28 .years old on March 1, 1956 . 
The last date of receipt of applications in the Ministry of Education is January 
l , 1958 . 

Necessary particulars regarding the scholarship and copies of the application form 
can be had from the Government of India, Ministry of Education . Scholiships Divi 
sions, Section 8-1, New Delhi and may also be seen from the Office of the As.istant 
Beoretary (Education ) Govt . of Manipur . 

Gopondra Sharma . 
Publicity Officer, Manipur,

মণ ১০ তলা) খক লৌজগনি । বিগে হায় মীনা মণ খুদিংদা লুপা কয়াস রেষ্টা পীব মগদগে হায়

গৰিৰ আগনি । টেণ্ডয় পীৰিগৰ মীনা অরনেষ্ট মিনি পা ২০ ( সা . ) ইল, ট্রেজরিপা থমন্তবগা চলান 
কলী অমগা লিনী পেলগ লােয়ননা টের পীবিগদৰনি ।
